10.1021_acsenergylett.5c03259: Enabling a nonexpensive, highly active, and durable anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) promises to meet the surging energy demand reducing the carbon footprint. Their major discrepancy is the poor durability of the oxidation compartment with a less-durable catalyst and electrode-support assembly. Unlike efficient expensive catalysts IrO 2 and RuO 2 in proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer, the anion-exchange ones use inexpensive 3d-transition-metal-based compounds as the anode electrocatalysts. These catalysts are poorly stable at ampere-level current density, because of metal leaching, surface passivation/insulation, mechanical instability, carbon-substrate degradation, side reactions by leached metal damaging the membrane, alkaline and oxidative degradation of the ionomer, and insufficient mass transfer due to poor bubble dynamics in alkaline media. Besides efficient material design, there are various other parameters that govern the electrolyzers’ longevity. This perspective focuses on the understanding and directions to solve each above-mentioned problem to attain more stable, durable, and highly active AEMWEs.
10.1021_acsnano.6c05789: Two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures offer tunable interlayer spacing and accessible surfaces that can overcome key limitations of conventional sodium-ion battery (SIBs) anodes. Here, we investigate Na+ storage mechanisms in three-layer 2D heterostructures composed of horizontally stacked graphene (G), nitrogen-doped graphene (NG), and MoS2 (M) by combining cyclic voltammetry with operando spectroelectrochemical Raman spectroscopy. Restricting the active thickness to three atomic layers enables direct spectroscopic access to interfacial charge transfer and strain during cycling. Electrochemical analysis reveals that Na+ storage is governed by two coupled factors: the permeability of the electrolyte-facing outer layer, and the electronic–mechanical interactions within the interlayer space. NG outer layers facilitate ion access and deliver up to 40-fold higher capacities than pristine graphene stacks, whereas MoS2 top layers suppress ion infiltration. Operando Raman correlates faradaic features with reversible structural changes, allowing separation of charge-doping and strain effects during cycling. The results demonstrate that Na+ storage proceeds predominantly via reversible accumulation in confined interlayer and blister-like reservoirs formed during solvent cointercalation. Incorporating MoS2 as a middle layer redistributes charge and buffers mechanical strain, enhancing cycling stability. These findings provide insights into charge storage mechanisms in 2D materials.
10.1039_d5ta10086k: This review summarizes recent advances in surface engineering for OER catalysts in direct seawater electrolysis, focusing on how surface-modulation enhances catalytic activity, corrosion resistance, and selectivity in harsh marine environments.
10.1039_d6ta02981g: Lithium loss during NMC cathode synthesis is dominated by substrate reactions, not Li 2 O evaporation. Moisture in the calcination atmosphere provides a secondary loss pathway via LiOH (g) formation.
